title: Pennsylvania's 9th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Pennsylvania's 9th Congressional District pits four-term Republican incumbent Dan Meuser against Democratic challenger Rachel Wallace. The district, which covers parts of 12 counties in northeastern and central Pennsylvania including Schuylkill, Berks, Lebanon, and Luzerne counties, is heavily Republican; former President Donald Trump carried it by a 38-point margin in 2024. Meuser, a former Pennsylvania Secretary of Revenue and business executive, is seeking re-election on a platform of conservative economic policies and border security. Wallace, a former White House Office of Management and Budget chief of staff and longtime public servant, is running on a platform focused on lowering healthcare costs, reducing the cost of living, and bringing federal investment back to the district. The Cook Political Report rates the race as Solidly Republican.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to the Pennsylvania 9th Congressional District general election were found as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid Republican,' and no recent independent polling has been published for this matchup.

candidates.name: Dan Meuser
candidates.summary: Dan Meuser is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 9th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. He previously served as Pennsylvania's Secretary of Revenue (2011-2015) and spent decades as a business executive at Pride Mobility Products. Meuser serves on the House Financial Services Committee and House Small Business Committee, and is a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus and the Republican Study Committee.

candidates.name: Rachel Wallace
candidates.summary: Rachel Wallace is a Democratic candidate for U.S. House in Pennsylvania's 9th Congressional District. A Pottsville native and ninth-generation Pennsylvanian, she previously served as Chief of Staff for the White House Office of Management and Budget (2021-2023) and held roles at the U.S. State Department, the U.S. Senate, and for former U.S. Representative Tim Holden. Her campaign focuses on lowering healthcare costs, reducing the cost of living, and bringing federal investment to the district.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific polling exists (based_on_poll_count=0), which tempers confidence. However, the non-polling data is overwhelmingly one-sided: four-term Republican incumbent Dan Meuser faces Democratic challenger Rachel Wallace in a district that Donald Trump carried by 38 points in 2024. The Cook Political Report rates the race as Solidly Republican. The district's strong Republican partisan baseline, combined with Meuser's incumbency advantage and lack of any contrary polling or credible threat signals in the race data, points to an extremely high likelihood of a Republican hold. Without polling, the margin estimate is approximate but consistent with the 38-point presidential baseline and a safe-r rating.
